post.description:
Exchanges the httpOnly refresh cookie (set at login) for a fresh 15-minute
access token, so a session survives past the access token's expiry for up to
`jwt_refresh_hours` of idleness (spec §8: "8 h idle"). The refresh cookie is
rotated on every call, which is what makes that window *idle*-based rather
than a hard cap from login.

Only a genuine `type: "refresh"` token is accepted here -- an access token can
never be replayed through this endpoint to mint new tokens (just as
get_current_asset_user refuses a refresh token used as an access token).
Role/company are re-read from the asset_user row, so a role change or
deactivation takes effect on the next refresh rather than living on in a
stale token.

Clears the refresh cookie so a logged-out browser can't silently mint a new
access token via /refresh for the rest of the refresh window. Unauthenticated
on purpose: logging out must work even with an already-expired access token.
S8: a LOGOUT row names the person when the refresh cookie still says who it was.

post.description:
An Employee, optionally able to sign in: `login.enabled`, `login.role` (ADMIN / OPERATOR / VIEWER /

(or Reset Password). Where the employee sits: `location_id`, or `location_name` (an existing place of that
company with that name, else a new one).

A Store (code: three letters, optionally one more letter or digit; login email from the store email
rule, able to sign in but with NO password until one is issued) together with its Stock Room and its
Install Point. Whatever already exists is reused (a store with this code, STK-<code>, INS-<code>), so
running it twice creates nothing new: 201 when something was created, 200 when everything existed.

Head-office admin: gives every active store (of one company, or all) the Stock Room and Install Point
it lacks. Nothing that exists is changed; a store whose room code is taken by something else is listed
in `problems` and the rest go ahead.

An Install Point (where things are fixed in place). Code made from the name (INS-...); it never signs
in. The same name again in the same company returns the existing one (200, `created: false`).

get.description:
`exact=true` makes `q` match whole identifiers (code or its last segment,
serial, barcode, ERP item code, PO/invoice/PI no) instead of any text containing it.
S5: without it `q` also finds the Item's, vendor's, brand's and holder's names (and the
holder's code), and -- when no sort column is chosen -- lists exact identifier matches
first, then values starting with the text, then the rest. New filters: `holder_type`
(employee / store / stock room / install point), `holder_id` (= `asset_user_id`),
`vendor_id`, `po_number` (whole PO number, any case), `work_area` (= `domain`).
Scoped exactly like `_get_scoped_asset`: a SELF_SERVICE asset_user only ever sees
assets they currently hold (so `asset_user_id` is pinned to their own id, ignoring
any value the caller passed, and the company filter is left unrestricted since
asset_user_id already narrows it); everyone else is scoped to `scoped_company_ids`
(None = ADMIN, unrestricted) AND `allowed_asset_domains` (None = ADMIN/SELF_SERVICE
unrestricted, spec §14/§15 -- an OPERATOR/VIEWER can never widen past their own
configured domain by passing a `domain` outside it, see search_assets). AM-21:
`sort_by` must be one of search_assets.SORTABLE_COLUMNS -- an unrecognized value is
silently ignored (falls back to the existing newest-first order) rather than a 422,
so an old cached frontend bundle or a stale saved link never breaks.

put.description:
AM-02: the first general edit surface for an asset's EDITABLE DESCRIPTIVE
DATA (see the Asset Field Policy Matrix in docs/ai/AM-02_ASSET_DATA_MODEL_REPORT.md)
-- previously there was no way to correct e.g. a mistyped serial number or
add a PI Number after the fact without going through a lifecycle event,
which this deliberately is not: no asset_event row is written, no status/
asset_user change happens, nothing here touches the ledger. Identity fields
(asset_code/company_id/cost_center_id) aren't in AssetUpdateIn at all --
trg_asset_no_identity_change would reject them at the database level even
if they were.

AM-04: required-active-custom-field completeness is only enforced when
this edit itself includes `custom_fields` -- an asset that predates a
newly-added required UDF must not be blocked from an unrelated edit (e.g.
fixing a serial number) solely because it has no value for that field
yet (docs/ai/DECISIONS.md). Also writes one AssetFieldChange row per
genuinely changed field, in the same transaction as the edit (committed
together below, never separately).

delete.description:
Soft-deletes an asset created by data-entry mistake. Only allowed while the asset
still has just its original PROCURED/IMPORTED event — once it has moved, been repaired
or been disposed, that history is real and must stay visible; use the DISPOSED/SCRAPPED/
LOST lifecycle events instead (spec §7 "nothing is hard-deleted").

get.description:
AM-04 §23: read surface for the field-change audit -- scoped exactly
like viewing the asset itself (same _get_scoped_asset), so a ASSET_USER sees
only their own asset's history and no cross-company leakage is possible.
Chronological, oldest first, matching the lifecycle Timeline's ordering.

schema.title: Response List Asset Changes Api Assets  Asset Id  Changes Get

put.description:
S4: settles the pending serials of many assets at once (the Serial Pending screen after a
receipt of 50 amplifiers): each entry a real serial, or `no_serial` (saved as N/A). Same rules as
PUT /{id}/serial -- company and work-area scope, the asset's serial must be pending, global
uniqueness (also among the entries themselves, any letter case; N/A never clashes), the same
field-change audit. Everything is checked first: any problem -> 422 `{detail, errors, problems:
[{entry_index, asset_id, serial?, message}]}` and nothing is saved; otherwise all are saved.

Settles an asset whose serial was pending: the serial read from the opened
box, or "no serial" when it turns out to have none (saved as N/A). Same scope as
any other asset edit (company and Responsibility), same global-uniqueness rule,
and the change is written to the field-change audit like an ordinary edit.

post.description:
AM-07: a deliberately separate, narrower operation from
`PUT /api/assets/{id}` for correcting Category, Subcategory, and/or
Purchase Date -- the three fields `AssetUpdateIn` has excluded since
AM-02 precisely because they're controlled master/date references, not
ordinary descriptive data. Same scoping as every other asset-mutation
endpoint (`_get_scoped_asset`): a ASSET_USER never reaches this route at all
(`require_role` gate), and IT_TEAM can only correct an asset already
inside their own company scope. `body.model_fields_set` is what tells
"this field wasn't part of the request" apart from "explicitly set to
null" -- see `AssetCorrectionIn`'s own docstring.

get.description:
Goes through the same `_get_scoped_asset` every other `/api/assets/{id}/...`
route uses (Task 16), so a ASSET_USER who doesn't currently hold this asset gets 404
here exactly like they would from GET /api/assets/{id} -- a QR code is not a
backdoor around asset scoping.

Print Labels (bulk physical tagging): a linear Code128 barcode
(default) or a QR code, either way encoding this asset's bare
`asset_code` -- deliberately NOT `/qr.png` above, which encodes a deep
link for a different purpose (open the asset's page) and is left
untouched. Same `_get_scoped_asset` scoping as every other
`/api/assets/{id}/...` route -- a label image is not a backdoor around
asset scoping either.

schema.title: Response List Events Api Assets  Asset Id  Events Get

get.description:
Staff only: a SELF_SERVICE asset_user sees only the assets they hold (spec §6),
never company-wide KPIs/alerts, so they get 403 here. Scoped exactly like the asset
register (Task 19): `scoped_company_ids` returns None for ADMIN (unrestricted,
sees every company combined) and the caller's own company id otherwise, so a
non-ADMIN never sees another company's KPI numbers. `domain` is the optional "My
Responsibility" selector (spec §37/§67) -- always further narrowed by the caller's
own `allowed_asset_domains` server-side, never trusted to widen past it.

Same filters and the exact same scoping branch as `GET /api/assets`
(`list_assets` in app.assets.router, Task 19): a ASSET_USER's `asset_user_id` is pinned to
their own id (so they only ever export the assets they currently hold, regardless
of any `asset_user_id`/`company_id` they pass in) and every other role is scoped by
`scoped_company_ids` (None = ADMIN, unrestricted; otherwise just their own
company) -- a non-ADMIN caller can never export another company's rows. `domain`
is the optional Responsibility filter (spec §38), same as the register's own --
always further bounded server-side by allowed_asset_domains, never a way to widen
past it (see search_assets). S5 (additive filters, shared with the preview): `work_area`
(= domain), `item_id`, `vendor_id`, `po_number` (whole number, any case), `holder_id`
(= asset_user_id), `purchase_from` / `purchase_to` (purchase date, inclusive).

The asset register report on screen: the same filters, scope and rows as GET /export/assets
(`columns` = the file's headings, each row a dict keyed by them, `asset_ids` in the same order), one
page at a time, plus `total` and a `summary` (count by status, by category, top 10 Items) over
everything the filters match.

The movement log on screen: the same query, scope and rows as GET /export/movements, one page at a
time (`columns` = the file's headings), plus `total`.

Staff only (403 for a ASSET_USER): the log names every asset_user in the company, and a
ASSET_USER may only see their own currently-held assets (spec §6). Company-scoped the
same way as the dashboard (`scoped_company_ids`): a non-ADMIN role only ever gets
movement rows for assets in their own company, ADMIN is unrestricted. Joins in the
asset code and the from/to asset_user names so the exported "Asset Code"/"From AssetUser"/
"To AssetUser" columns hold what they say, not raw internal ids.

AM-06 §22/§25: the field-change audit (`asset_field_change`, AM-04's
append-only edit trail) gets its own export -- a separate canonical
dataset from both the asset register (current snapshot) and the
movement log (`asset_event`), never flattened into either (see
docs/ai/DECISIONS.md). Staff only (ASSET_USER gets 403, same as the
movement log -- the audit names every actor in the company, and a
ASSET_USER may only see their own currently-held assets per spec §6),
company-scoped the same way as every other report here.

PO (409, "Cancel the waiting items instead": POST /{id}/cancel-waiting).
S0.3: someone limited to one work area may only delete a PO whose lines
are all in their own area (deleting cancels every line).

serial pending, under repair, lost (everyone); unlinked-to-Item assets (ADMIN); POs / units waiting for
goods (ADMIN, OPERATOR); ERP changed POs, goods arrived not yet received, ERP POs needing input (ADMIN,
OPERATOR, when the ERP link is set up); the ERP inbox counts (head-office admin). A number the caller
is not meant to see is null. `work_area` (IT / Non-IT) narrows the CKAM figures inside the caller's own
area; `include_erp=false` skips the ERP figures.

`group=true`: one row per fingerprint {fingerprint, exception_type, message, level, kind, count,
first_seen, last_seen, last_request_id, sample_route}, most recent first.

The audit history of one record (e.g. /entity/vendor/12, /entity/asset_user/5), newest first: every
DATA change and every SECURITY / ACCESS / LIFECYCLE row that names it.

Everything that carries one request id: {request_id, found, audit, security, errors, system,
client_reports, access_log}. A client report's `reference` is found here too.

Streams the rows of one log for a period (oldest first), at most 100,000 (the header
`X-Row-Count` says how many; `X-Truncated: true` when there were more). Redacted again on the way out.
The export itself is an EXPORT audit row.

Everything needed to understand a problem, redacted: version, migration state, safe config, ERP copy,
database health, table counts, the last 20 error groups with stacks, security and system events, new
client reports, slow requests / SQL, and (with `request_id`) that request's whole story. `markdown` is
the same as one text to paste into a chat.

AssetBatchIn.title: AssetBatchIn
AssetBatchIn.description:
S5: POST /api/assets/batch -- add `quantity` assets of one Item in one go. Category, sub-category and
work area come from the Item; the company from the cost centre; brand, warranty, serial rule and
description default from the Item. Everything is checked first; see app.assets.batch.

AssetCorrectionIn.title: AssetCorrectionIn
AssetCorrectionIn.description:
AM-07: a dedicated, narrower request shape for
`POST /api/assets/{id}/corrections` -- deliberately NOT part of
`AssetUpdateIn`/`PUT /api/assets/{id}`. Every field except `reason` is
optional (a correction may touch just Category, just Purchase Date, or
any combination); which of `category_id`/`subcategory_id`/
`purchase_date` were actually included in the request body at all
(`model_fields_set`) is what the router/service use to tell "not part
of this correction" apart from "explicitly set to null" -- the second
only being meaningful for `subcategory_id`, since Category and Purchase
Date can never legitimately be cleared.

AssetCreateIn.title: AssetCreateIn
AssetCreateIn.description:
Purchase Date is deliberately NOT a field here -- per business rule
(docs/ai/DECISIONS.md), it is always Invoice Date when Invoice Date is
given, and is derived by the router (never accepted from the client),
exactly like the Purchase Order delivery path already derives it from
Invoice Date too. AM-19: PO/Invoice/PI No+Date are now OPTIONAL here --
ground reality is that Invoice (and sometimes even PO) paperwork often
isn't in hand yet when the physical asset is being logged, and PI
specifically always arrives later from Finance; each can be filled in
afterward via ordinary Edit. When Invoice Date is left blank, Purchase
Date falls back to today's date (the day the asset is logged) instead
-- see app.assets.router.create_asset. Category/Sub-Category/Vendor
remain mandatory (always known at entry time in practice). This
deliberately does NOT touch the PO/Pending Asset entry path's own
fields, nor AM-07's correction workflow.

AM-19: `quantity` is gone -- every submission creates exactly one
asset now (a quantity>1 batch only ever worked for the "N/A" no-serial
case anyway, since a real Serial Number can't be shared; Import is the
correct tool for a genuine multi-unit bulk add).

AssetDetailOut.title: AssetDetailOut
AssetDetailOut.description:
AM-04: Asset 360 needs human-readable labels, not bare IDs (§25 of the
AM-04 authorization) -- additive-only, single-asset GET response.
Nullable everywhere a referenced master row could theoretically be
missing (defensive; scoping/FKs should prevent this in practice). Adds
every remaining label the list endpoint's own page-scoped batch lookup
(AM-11, current_asset_user_name/company_name on AssetOut itself) does not
already cover, since a single-asset page can afford a few more small
lookups that a paginated list of up to 200 rows should not repeat.

AssetOut.title: AssetOut
AssetOut.description:
AM-02: expanded to mirror the Asset model's business/procurement fields --
these were already captured correctly on create (AssetCreateIn already had
them; the columns and migration already existed from the original build)
but were never returned to any client, so nothing in the frontend could
ever display vendor/PO/invoice/PI/brand/model/serial/warranty/custom
fields even though they were being saved. Purely additive to the response
contract; existing consumers (which only read the previously-exposed
subset) are unaffected.

AssetSubcategoryEditIn.title: AssetSubcategoryEditIn
AssetSubcategoryEditIn.description:
`category_id`/`code` omitted deliberately -- both immutable after
creation (AM-05): re-parenting a subcategory to a different category
wasn't proven safe against existing asset code_rule tokens/history.

AssetUpdateIn.title: AssetUpdateIn
AssetUpdateIn.description:
The EDITABLE DESCRIPTIVE DATA subset only -- see the Asset Field Policy
Matrix in docs/ai/AM-02_ASSET_DATA_MODEL_REPORT.md. Deliberately excludes:
asset_code/company_id/cost_center_id (DB-trigger immutable), status/
current_asset_user_id/status_since (lifecycle-controlled, apply_event only),
category_id/subcategory_id/purchase_date (controlled master/date
references -- not yet exposed via generic edit, see the report), and
initial_asset_user_id (create-only, meaningless on an existing row).
A PUT replaces this whole editable subset in one call, matching this
codebase's existing convention (e.g. AssetUserIn on `PUT /api/asset-users/{id}`)
rather than a partial-PATCH merge.

AssetUserUpdateIn.title: AssetUserUpdateIn
AssetUserUpdateIn.description:
S1: PUT /asset-users/{id}. Every field is optional: a field LEFT OUT
keeps its stored value (so an edit form that does not show the work area
can no longer reset it); a field sent as null / blank clears it where that
is allowed (company, code, name, type and location can never be cleared).

BulkActionIn.title: BulkActionIn
BulkActionIn.description:
AM-20: the Asset Movement console -- scan a batch of assets by Serial
Number/Asset Code, pick ONE action and (for the actions that need one) ONE
destination AssetUser for the whole batch, apply to all of them at once.
`event_type` is any of actionRules.ts's own set (MOVED/SENT_FOR_REPAIR/
LOST/DISPOSED/SOLD/SCRAPPED/RECEIVED_FROM_REPAIR/FOUND) -- the backend
state machine (app.lifecycle.state_machine.transition) remains the real
authority on which is actually legal from each asset's current status,
exactly as it already is for the single-asset action buttons.

BundleLinesIn.title: BundleLinesIn
BundleLinesIn.description:
Add a bundle to a PO: `quantity` bundles at `price` each (before tax)
become one ordinary line per part, `quantity` units each. `parts` carries
the user's (possibly edited) amount per part; when omitted the server
splits `price` by the bundle's shares. Either way the part amounts must
add up to `price`.

ChangeActionIn.title: ChangeActionIn
ChangeActionIn.description: One difference from the ERP: apply it to this PO, or keep the PO as it is.

CostCenterEditIn.title: CostCenterEditIn
CostCenterEditIn.description:
`company_id`/`code` omitted deliberately -- both immutable after
creation (AM-05): the company relationship is a controlled boundary
(see `DEVELOPMENT_GUARDRAILS.md`/`DECISIONS.md`) and the code is the
identifier every referencing asset relies on.

CustomFieldEditIn.title: CustomFieldEditIn
CustomFieldEditIn.description:
`field_key`/`field_type` omitted deliberately -- both immutable after
creation (AM-05 §22): asset values are stored keyed by field_key, and
changing field_type could invalidate values already stored under the
old type. `company_id` (scope) is accepted here but the router only
honors a change to it when no asset currently holds a value for this
field_key -- see `masters/router.py`.

DepartmentEditIn.title: DepartmentEditIn
DepartmentEditIn.description:
Department has no separate business code -- `name` itself is the
unique identifier, but nothing else in the system keys off its exact
string value (AssetUser.department_id is a stable FK), so renaming it is a
safe descriptive edit, not an identity change.

ErpVendorLinkIn.title: ErpVendorLinkIn
ErpVendorLinkIn.description: An ERP supplier of one company (the same code means a different supplier in each company).

ImportCommitOut.title: ImportCommitOut
ImportCommitOut.description:
AM-23: `imported`/`updated` (asset import's Add/Edit modes),
`pos_created`/`lines_created` (PO import), and `moved` (movement
import) are all mutually exclusive by which endpoint responded --
every field is optional so one shape serves all of them rather than a
separate response model per import type.

InboxItemDecisionIn.title: InboxItemDecisionIn
InboxItemDecisionIn.description:
One decision of the ERP inbox: for an Article (`article_key`, scope ARTICLE) or one code (`icode`,
scope CODE / NAME / ARTICLE), in one company: an existing Item, a new Item, or not tracked.

IssuePasswordsIn.title: IssuePasswordsIn
IssuePasswordsIn.description:
S5: POST /asset-users/issue-passwords -- a temporary password for many accounts at once (e.g. every new
store). Choose the accounts by id, or by kind and/or company.

ItemSetPartIn.title: ItemSetPartIn
ItemSetPartIn.description: S6: one part of the set an Item is made of ("CPU", the Item CPU, 70%).

LineGroupOut.title: LineGroupOut
LineGroupOut.description:
One PO line: every unit sharing a line number, counted over the units
the caller may see. ordered = received + waiting.

LineGroupUpdateIn.title: LineGroupUpdateIn
LineGroupUpdateIn.description:
Edit a whole line. Only the fields sent are changed (the rest keep the
line's current values); the same limits as editing one unit apply.
`quantity` is the new ORDERED total (received + waiting).

LocationEditIn.title: LocationEditIn
LocationEditIn.description:
`company_id`/`code` omitted deliberately -- both immutable after
creation (AM-05), same rule as CostCenter's own edit schema.

NotTrackedIn.title: NotTrackedIn
NotTrackedIn.description:
S3a-2: mark a line of an ERP PO "not tracked" from the review (CODE / NAME / ARTICLE; the three broad
levels only for the head-office admin).

PoWithLinesLineIn.title: PoWithLinesLineIn
PoWithLinesLineIn.description:
One line of the one-screen manual PO: the Item decides category, sub-category, work area and serial
mode; description / brand / warranty default from the Item when left out; barcode is optional.

PoWithLinesSetIn.title: PoWithLinesSetIn
PoWithLinesSetIn.description:
One set (bundle) of the one-screen manual PO: `quantity` sets at `price_per_set` each (before tax),
one line per part (`part_amounts` = the amount per part, else the bundle's own split).

PurchaseOrderUpdateIn.title: PurchaseOrderUpdateIn
PurchaseOrderUpdateIn.description: S6: PUT /api/purchase-orders/{id} -- only the fields sent change (see app.purchase_orders.header).

PurchaseOrderWithLinesIn.title: PurchaseOrderWithLinesIn
PurchaseOrderWithLinesIn.description: S3a-2: a whole manual PO in one call -- header, lines and sets, all or nothing.

PurchaseOrderWithLinesOut.title: PurchaseOrderWithLinesOut
PurchaseOrderWithLinesOut.description:
The new PO (same shape as GET /purchase-orders/{id}) plus what was created: lines (line numbers;
a set counts one per part) and units.

ReceiveIn.title: ReceiveIn
ReceiveIn.description:
S4: a receipt against a purchase order. The common fields are entered once; the PO's delivery
place is used when `received_into_asset_user_id` is left out.

ReceiveLineIn.title: ReceiveLineIn
ReceiveLineIn.description:
One line of a receipt: how many of its waiting units arrive now (the server takes the oldest
waiting ones), and their serials when the line has them.

RecordPiIn.title: RecordPiIn
RecordPiIn.description:
AM-19: PI arrives per Invoice, not per PO -- a PO delivered across
several partial deliveries gets one Invoice (and later one PI) per
delivery, never a single PI for the whole PO. See
app.purchase_orders.service.record_pi_for_invoice.

SerialBulkIn.title: SerialBulkIn
SerialBulkIn.description: S4: PUT /api/assets/serials -- fill the pending serials of many assets at once, all or nothing.

SerialEntryIn.title: SerialEntryIn
SerialEntryIn.description: S4: one entry of a bulk serial fill -- the asset, and its serial (or no_serial).

SerialFillIn.title: SerialFillIn
SerialFillIn.description:
Fills in the serial of an asset whose serial was pending: a real serial,
or no_serial=true when it turns out to have none (saved as N/A).

SyncRunOut.title: SyncRunOut
SyncRunOut.description: One run of the copy of the ERP data (see app.erp.sync).

VendorChoiceIn.title: VendorChoiceIn
VendorChoiceIn.description:
S3a-2: how to match the PO's ERP supplier when it is not linked yet -- done inside the PO's own
transaction. LINK = to an existing vendor (`vendor_id`); CREATE = a new vendor from the ERP supplier
(`name` optional, else the ERP's). `also_link_codes`: other registrations of the same supplier (same PAN)
in the same company, linked to the same vendor.

VendorCodesIn.title: VendorCodesIn
VendorCodesIn.description: S3a-2: several ERP suppliers (registrations) of ONE company.

VendorEditIn.title: VendorEditIn
VendorEditIn.description:
AM-05 safe-edit schema: `code` (the immutable identifier -- already
referenced by every asset that names this vendor) is deliberately not
declared here, so sending it in a PUT body is simply ignored, the same
convention AssetUpdateIn already established for asset_code.
